release.body:
Pandafish now continues selective quiescence for up to 16 ordinary tactical plies, with the existing four extra check-evasion plies. Static exchange evaluation filters losing non-checking ordinary captures outside check; checking captures, promotions, and evasions remain eligible. Evaluation, main search, clocks, transposition rules, and root tie handling are unchanged.

The exchange estimate follows legal least-valuable recaptures and accounts for pins, x-rays, king safety, en passant, and promotions. It remains a material heuristic and can miss sacrifices with compensation elsewhere; finite search caps can still stop unresolved tactics.

The tested **v0.13-dev** candidate completed 100 serial games per opponent:

| Opponent | W / D / L | Unfinished | Forfeits | Completed score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v0.12 | 46 / 43 / 11 | 0 | 0 | 67.5% |
| Stockfish Skill 1 | 58 / 11 / 31 | 0 | 0 | 63.5% |
| Sacrifice v0.2.0 b528f0ba | 24 / 28 / 48 | 0 | 0 | 38% |

No unfinished games or forfeits occurred in all 300 games. The separate v0.12 screens scored 57.5% against Skill 1 and 17.5% against Sacrifice; these are promising screening results, not a precise Elo estimate or guaranteed gain at every time control. The maximum candidate response was 136.474 ms, within the 150-ms deadline including protocol allowance.

Validation: focused SEE and legal-recapture oracle tests, full Go tests and race checks, vet, ARM64 build, offline lichess-bot wrapper with 12 legal plies, config validation, and short serial release integration matches against all three opponents. No live games were played for verification.

[Complete method, identities, hashes, timings, raw PGNs, and limitations](https://github.com/philyawj/Pandafish/blob/v0.13/tools/benchmark/results/v0.13-dev-vs-v0.12-and-stockfish-1-and-sacrifice-v0.2.0-b528f0ba/README.md). Original development labels and hashes are retained. Release preparation changes version text and documentation only; Stockfish Skill 1 remains the routine target.
